9d7f8d227962d5a1: MUNICH: Already ravaged by injuries, Bayern Munich head to Lille in the Champions League on Wednesday swept up in a firestorm of their own making over star midfielder Jamal Musiala.
Currently 13th in the table, Bayern need points if they are to reach the top eight and avoid a punishing extra knockout round.
While Lille are languishing in 35th spot and last season's semi-finalists Bayern limp into the clash despite being one of the leading contenders.
Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane was the latest to join Bayern's bulging casualty ward with an ankle injury on Friday which will likely rule him out until February.
But while Musiala returned after a two-month absence in last week's match, club bosses were accused of launching a coordinated effort to pressure the midfielder into accepting a pay cut.
That the club decided to kick-start the furore a day before announcing record revenues of close to a billion euros has not gone unnoticed.
- 'Own goal' -
In August, Musiala revealed he was suffering from a "neurological disorder" which can lead to "temporary but treatable seizures", having collapsed twice on the field in pre-season.

After his return, club powerbroker Karl-Heinz Rummenigge told German TV the 23-year-old midfielder was unlikely to recapture his previous form due to the condition – and should consider taking a pay cut.

"If he doesn't return to being the Jamal of old, then we need to have a conversation with his family, with the player, and, above all, with his agency – because, frankly, the current financial figures would no longer be justifiable," Rummenigge told Sky Germany.
Rummenigge's statements were striking but echoed those made by former president and fellow powerbroker Uli Hoeness, along with current CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen.
On Sunday, player union FIFPRO slammed Bayern, accusing the club of a "coordinated campaign to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives" to accept a wage cut.
"A club of Bayern's standing should know better," FIFPRO said in a statement.
FIFPRO's German counterparts VDV joined the chorus on Monday, saying the comments would "leave a lasting impression" on Musiala and on the club in general.
"I believe those in charge have scored a real 'own goal' here," VDV president Carsten Ramelow said in a statement.
World Cup and Ballon d'Or winner Lothar Matthaeus, who has never been afraid to butt heads with Hoeness and the Bayern brass, said the club should provide Musiala with "every bit of support."
"Right now, everything is being placed on Musiala's shoulders," Matthaeus told RTL.
"Perhaps all parties can sit down and talk later at a more opportune moment," he added.
- An opportunity for Musiala -
For their part, Bayern coach Vincent Kompany and powerful sporting director Max Eberl have thrown their support behind Musiala publicly.
Kompany, who himself returned on Friday from a month out after being hospitalised with meningeal irritation in October, backed Musiala.
"The coach must be the one to believe in the player. And if we manage to bring him back, then everyone wins: the club, the fans – and all of German football."
Eberl said on Friday he was confident Musiala would return to his best form if given the chance.
Bayern's injury crisis has provided Musiala with an opportunity to illustrate his importance to the club by starring in the coming months.
Besides Kane, Serge Gnabry, Alphonso Davies, Ismael Saibari and captain Manuel Neuer will miss Wednesday's match.
Michael Olise and Luis Diaz are also injury doubts, meaning the only recognised fit forward is 18-year-old winger Lennart Karl.
Musiala has not addressed the controversy directly, but gave an insight into how he shuts out pressure and critique at a fan event this weekend.
Asked by a fan how he handled the weight of expectation, Musiala said he was still in the process of finding the right approach.
"I'm still learning... Too much pressure isn't good, but a hunger for victory is important," Musiala said.
"Finding that balance is a very important part of life." - AFP

556ccf60529b10ea: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is gearing up for the first major overhaul of its equity benchmark in 17 years, a shake-up that may channel more investor money into technology and energy companies just as traders rethink the profitability of the AI trade.

The FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) will expand to 50 stocks from 30, with new constituents selected based on full market capitalization and other criteria. The additions will be announced Dec 3, ahead of a phased inclusion beginning later that month.

“The broader index gives investors a better representation of the Malaysian economy beyond just banks, plantations and utilities,” said Danny Wong, chief executive officer of Areca Capital. “Over a longer period, when the earnings growth and currency turn more attractive, this will improve the interest in KLCI.”

The revamp may reshape investment flows and reduce the benchmark’s reliance on banks and utilities, which account for nearly 60% of the index’s weight. FTSE Russell simulations suggest technology, energy and real estate companies may be added, potentially attracting more foreign money while increasing exposure to AI volatility and tighter US technology restrictions.

Malaysia’s export-driven economy has been a major beneficiary of the AI boom, with shipments reaching a record this year and electrical and electronic products accounting for more than half of the total.

Long a base for packaging and testing semiconductors for global companies, Malaysia is now seeking to develop its own chips. It has also emerged as one of Southeast Asia’s leading data centre hubs, drawing investment from Oracle and Amazon to Alibaba and ByteDance.

That expansion has created a range of picks-and-shovels AI trades, including utility YTL Power International Bhd, which has a data centre partnership with Nvidia, and grid operator Tenaga Nasional Bhd.

The benchmark overhaul may change how global funds gain exposure to those themes in 2027. Investors may increasingly look to Southeast Asian markets where valuations are more attractive, HSBC Holdings Plc strategists including Herald van der Linde wrote in a note.

The shift comes with growing risks. The US earlier this month announced new restrictions on data centre operators in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia as President Donald Trump steps up efforts to curb China’s access to advanced chips. The FBM KLCI has also fallen around 8% this year amid US$1.8 billion of foreign outflows.
Still, with the index “drifting towards our bear case, we believe there are opportunities to bargain hunt,” Lim Sue Lin, head of research at Maybank Investment Bank, wrote in a note this month.

FTSE Russell simulations indicate the revamped benchmark may include Alliance Bank Malaysia, Dialog Group, Frontken Corp. and Genting Malaysia, as well as IGB Real Estate Investment Trust. Any resulting flows may unfold over several months, with the 20 additions entering at half their eventual weights on Dec 21 before moving to full weight in June 2027, creating two windows for portfolio adjustments.

Investors have broadly welcomed the expansion, according to Khoi Vu, lead Asean equity strategist at JPMorgan Chase & Co. The broader index should better reflect Malaysia’s economy and lead to “greater fund flows and coverage for lesser-known stocks,” he said.

97e43ef44e8d072f: KUALA LUMPUR: Ten years into his marriage to Datin Sharifah Ladyana Syed Shamsuddin, Malaysian rock icon Datuk Awie has decided not to have any more children.
Instead, he wants to focus on rekindling the romance with his wife and enjoying family life.

Speaking at the couple's lively 10th wedding anniversary party last Sunday night, the 58-year-old Wings frontman—born Ahmad Azhar Othman—shared that raising seven children from his current and previous marriages makes his life feel complete.

"The hope is that we just want to be happy. I want to work, raise those two little warriors (Putra Ahmad Andeeka and Putra Ahmad Arjunna), and see Qasseh (Putri Qasseh Antasha) and Rezzki (Putra Ahmad Rezzki) through school. Praise be to God, that is all," he said.

Ever the joker, the veteran rocker added that it was high time he and Ladyana made quality time for each other. "Seven (children) are enough. Give me a chance to rest and fall in love all over again with my wife. We have made many sacrifices. God willing, moving forward, I want to enjoy life with my family," he quipped.
The milestone celebration, which took two months to organise, was Awie's way of thanking his wife for her dedication to their family over the past decade.
Hoping their marriage lasts a lifetime, he said, "I did this in remembrance of my wife's sacrifices over 10 years, taking care of my children during that period."
The evening took an emotional turn when all seven of Awie's children went on stage together to share heartfelt tributes to the couple.

His five older children from previous marriages to Arni Nazira and Rozana Misbun—Putri Aleeya Antasha, 26, Putri Aleefa Antasha, 24, Putra Ahmad Merrah, 19, Putra Ahmad Rezzki, 18, and Putri Qasseh Antasha, 16—were joined by his two youngest boys with Ladyana, Putra Ahmad Andeeka, 6, and Putra Ahmad Arjunna, 2.
To cap off the night, Awie surprised Ladyana with jewellery for her 39th birthday on Nov 22.
The event also celebrated the 11th anniversary of the Wings Motor Gang Society (WMGS), a biking club united by their love for the legendary band.
3f0e862838c53442: MANCHESTER: Enzo Maresca said Monday that a "reset" at Manchester City was inevitable following the end of Pep Guardiola's trophy-laden era as he looks to arrest a worrying slump in form.
City flew out of the blocks this season but have won just one of their past six matches in all competitions, excluding their League Cup penalty-shootout victory over Brighton.
The picture in Europe is rosier – Maresca's men are aiming for a fourth win in five Champions League matches when they host Napoli on Tuesday.
City boss Maresca, who was Guardiola's assistant during the club's treble-winning campaign of 2022/23, replaced the Spaniard in the hot seat ahead of the current season.
"For me, you know, this is like a reset, it's like a restart," he said at his pre-match press conference.

"After, we said already many times, but after 10 years, you know, with the same manager, same face, same words, same method, same... it's not easy to suddenly... now all of a sudden we change. So for me personally, it's all normal."
Maresca tweaked his midfield for Saturday's home game against Fulham, dropping Enzo Fernandez to the bench and bringing in Ayyoub Bouaddi to start alongside Elliot Anderson.
But City could only manage a 1-1 draw, meaning they have taken just one point from their past four Premier League games to fall six points behind leaders Arsenal.
Despite the rough run of results, the Italian urged patience, saying it would take time to learn his best options.
"Obviously it's not complicated," said Maresca. "It's just a matter, you know, to know each other.
"I need to understand who is the ideal one for these kind of games, who is the ideal one for different kind of games.
"I don't think it's just midfield. Also, we are trying, you know, with the defensive players, we are trying to find the right solution."
City winger Jeremy Doku is confident the team are heading in the right direction despite their recent stumbles.
Asked how long it would take for things to click, he said: "I don't think there's a time, we've done it pretty well.
"It's not because we won seven games (in the Premier League) that everything is good and lost a couple that everything is bad.
"I would say there is no timeline, but we're going in the right direction.
"Every day we're getting to know each other better, and in one moment it will click again and we'll be in full flow."
City's players could come up against club great Kevin De Bruyne when they face Napoli at the Etihad.
Maresca described the Belgian midfielder, who moved to the Italian club in 2025, as one of the best players in City's history.
"In the last 10 years, all the trophies the club has achieved. Kevin was here, was an important player, fantastic player, top guy," he said. - AFP

c7f3cd7754b1d046: MIRI: The public has been advised to exercise caution near rivers and waterways during the crocodile mating season, which runs from November to March each year.
The reminder by Sarawak Forestry Corporation (SFC) follows a crocodile attack on a worker at a floating jetty in Kuala Baram here on Sunday.

SFC Miri regional manager Louis Velda Dominic said preliminary investigations found that the incident occurred at 9.30pm when the victim was standing at the edge of the floating jetty in the port area.
He said the victim was rescued by two colleagues who witnessed the attack.
"The victim suffered injuries to his hand and buttocks and was rushed to a private hospital for further treatment," he said when contacted.
Louis said crocodiles could become more active and aggressive during the mating season.
He advised the public to keep a safe distance from the reptiles and avoid actions that could provoke them, particularly near rivers, lakes and waterways.
"Safety measures include not approaching or disturbing crocodiles, not feeding them and always obeying 'Beware of Crocodiles' warning signs in high-risk areas.
"Members of the public are also advised not to go alone and to remain alert near riverbanks, particularly between dusk and early morning, when crocodiles are actively hunting for food," he said.
The public is also encouraged to download the Sarawak Croc Watch application for information on crocodile sightings and high-risk areas.
For information or complaints about crocodiles in Miri, the public can contact the SFC Miri hotline at 019-8290994.

919728780dc96215: LONDON: Keane Lewis-Potter struck twice as Brentford battered 10-man Everton 4-0 to climb into the Premier League's top six on Monday.
Lewis-Potter's luck was in as twice he saw deflected efforts leave Jordan Pickford stranded before a wild challenge by captain James Tarkowski left Everton a man down for over half the match.

Vitaly Janelt's stunning strike from long range and Fabio Carvalho rounded off a comfortable victory for the Bees, who will fancy their chances when they travel to struggling Manchester United on Saturday.
"It'll probably go a bit under the radar because of the sending off but 11 versus 11 we were outstanding," said Brentford boss Keith Andrews.
"I'm really happy with the group, the club and long may it continue.
"Long way to go. Onto Old Trafford on Saturday and we're really looking forward to it."
David Moyes's record 593rd game as Everton boss was not one the Scot will want to remember as his side were swatted aside in west London despite having the chance to go fifth in the table.
"With two shots, both deflected in and took the goalkeeper the wrong way, and the third goal was a worldie outside the box. We could use them as excuses but there's no excuses tonight," said Moyes.
"The performance was way below the standards we've set and the way we've been playing recently."
A defensive mix-up allowed Jaidon Anthony too much time to pick out Lewis-Potter for the opening goal and his shot deflected off Jarrad Branthwaite to wrong-foot Pickford.
Two minutes later, Everton failed to deal with a free-kick into the box and Lewis-Potter was given two opportunities to double his tally.
The winger's first effort was blocked by Tarkowski before Thierno Barry this time deflected into his own net as the Frenchman threw himself towards the ball.
Worse was to come for the visitors when their skipper was shown red after a VAR review for catching Yehor Yarmoliuk on the shin.
Tarkowski will now be banned for Sunday's Merseyside derby at home to Liverpool.
Moyes turned to Jack Grealish off the bench at half-time in his first appearance since being dropped for breaching club discipline a month ago.
Grealish could do little to inspire the 10 men as Janelt's strike lit up an otherwise uneventful second half.
The German midfielder blasted into the top corner from well outside the box 23 minutes from time.
Carvalho rounded off the scoring from point-blank range when a corner fell to the former Liverpool winger in the 90th minute.
Brentford will head to Old Trafford for Mauricio Pochettino's first home match in charge of United full of confidence and eager to inflict more woe on the Red Devils.
United sit second bottom of the table after a nine-game winless league run, plunging the English giants into danger of being relegated for the first time in 52 years. - AFP

fb96b82c56e19494: SINGAPORE: The dollar hovered near a 20-month high on Tuesday, after Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia's chief executive officer breathed new life into the artificial intelligence (AI) rally and stoked expectations that the recovery would give the Federal Reserve greater scope to raise interest rates further.

Against the resurgent greenback, the euro languished near an over 18-month low at US$1.0907 after sliding 0.6 per cent overnight, while sterling similarly struggled to rebound from a one-year low and last traded at US$1.3037.
The dollar firmed to 104.32 against a basket of currencies, having peaked at 104.53 in the previous session.

Nvidia on Monday reinstated Huang as chief executive officer under pressure from US President Donald Trump, a stunning reversal following his resignation over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with a person alleged to be a Chinese spy.
The move reignited AI euphoria and sparked a blistering rally across equities, with Nvidia adding roughly US$950 billion to its market capitalisation overnight.

"It's really hard to say what Jensen Huang's comeback as the chief executive officer of Nvidia means to the whole AI investment boom, but judging by the equity market movement, investors seem pretty excited about his reinstatement and markets are buying into the whole AI narrative again," said Carol Kong, a currency strategist at Commonwealth Bank of Australia.
"For now, it seems to be a positive for the AI narrative that has been a crucial pillar of the US exceptionalism story that has supported the US dollar."
Traders have now fully priced in a 25-basis-point Fed rate hike next month and see a slim chance of an outsized 50-basis-point move, up from zero a day earlier, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

The equity market rout over the past week, led by a heavy sell-off in technology and chip stocks, had prompted investors to pare back bets on further Fed rate hikes amid uncertainty over how much more tightening the economy could withstand.

"Our US economists have been flagging that tighter financial conditions and lower equity valuations could limit the Fed's appetite for further tightening, though (Monday's) move is reversing some of that pressure," said Citi markets analyst Preston Pagli.
The yen eased slightly to 159.06 per dollar in early Asian trade, while the Australian dollar was pinned near an 11-month low at US$0.6627.
The New Zealand dollar similarly struggled at US$0.5450, not far from Monday's 17-year low of US$0.5434.

The Australian dollar has come under immense pressure in recent sessions following a repricing of domestic interest rate expectations, with markets now fully pricing in a rate cut next August and a total of 50 basis points worth of easing by the end of 2027.

Analysts at JPMorgan said in a note that short positions in the Australian dollar against the greenback have "accumulated substantially", with bearish positioning reaching "extreme levels in some cases" by their metrics.

"Looking first at options, AUD puts have been outnumbering calls for several months now. Early in this process, it seemed reasonable to assume that this might simply be macro hedging, rather than actual outright directional positioning. But the flows have probably migrated to the latter of late," they said.

1fc523dbc3723522: BENGALURU: Gold prices rose slightly on Tuesday, extending a rebound from a 14-month low as bargain hunters returned after last week's sharp sell-off, with investors awaiting US inflation data for fresh signals on the Federal Reserve's interest rate outlook.
Spot gold rose 0.4 per cent to US$3,645.29 an ounce by 0023 GMT, while US gold futures for December delivery fell 0.2 per cent to US$3,644.70.

New York Fed President John Williams said on Monday that persistently high inflation continues to point the US central bank towards tighter monetary policy, while stressing that the pace of future rate hikes will depend on incoming economic data.
The US Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) Index, a key gauge closely watched by the central bank as it targets a 2 per cent inflation rate, is due on Wednesday.

Markets are pricing in a 95 per cent chance of a 25-basis-point rate increase at the Fed's policy meeting in December, while a larger 50-basis-point hike is priced in at 4.9 per cent, according to CME's FedWatch tool.
Higher interest rates increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion, reducing its appeal to investors.
US stocks soared on Monday after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive officer following pressure from US President Donald Trump.

A European Central Bank rate hike next month may not be enough to fully contain inflation, but a follow-up move is not urgent given that worrying second-round effects are building only gradually, Lithuanian policymaker Gediminas Simkus said.
Among other metals, spot silver climbed 1.2 per cent to US$43.55 an ounce, platinum gained 0.4 per cent to US$1,330.42 and palladium rose 0.6 per cent to US$898.95.

29a058eea00b37ea: PETALING JAYA: The Securities Commission Malaysia (SC) is assessing trading in shares of NexG Bhd, now known as Datasonic Group Bhd, after a surge in price and volume around reports of a possible government takeover of its passport and MyKad supplier unit.

The finance ministry, which referred to the company by its former name, said the SC was obtaining and reviewing the relevant documents and information to determine whether there is sufficient basis for further action under the Capital Markets and Services Act 2007 (CMSA).
"If trading misconduct or any CMSA breach is detected and proven, the SC will take appropriate action," it said in a written parliamentary reply to Yeo Bee Yin (PH-Puchong).

1ae0e86b78e600f7: KUALA LUMPUR: KJTS Group Bhd's RM68 million data centre contract from Gamuda Engineering Sdn Bhd brings its total awards from the group to RM116 million.

The scope covers engineering, procurement, manufacturing, delivery, installation, testing and commissioning of mechanical systems, which CIMB Securities believes are primarily cooling systems.

CIMB Securities said data centres require continuous cooling to keep servers operating, potentially allowing cooling service providers to generate income beyond the initial installation and construction phase.

Unlike conventional mechanical, electrical and plumbing contractors that typically rely on project-based work, KJTS' cooling energy capabilities could allow it to pursue recurring service contracts after projects are completed.

"Given the energy-intensive operations and continuous cooling requirements of data centres, these opportunities could extend earnings contributions well beyond the initial engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning (EPCC) phase," CIMB Securities said.
The firm maintained its earnings forecasts for KJTS for financial years 2026 to 2028, as the latest contract awards were already accounted for in its assumptions.
It reiterated its "Buy" call on the stock with an unchanged target price of RM1.65, based on 25 times its estimated earnings for calendar year 2027.
At RM0.95, the target price implies potential upside of about 73.7 per cent.

"Nevertheless, we view the successive wins positively, as they demonstrate KJTS's ability to secure larger EPCC contracts and strengthen its position in the growing cooling energy market," the firm added.
KJTS provides cooling energy, cleaning and facilities management services, with its business also encompassing energy-as-a-service solutions.

bd4c7b05888ef9be: SINGAPORE: The dollar hovered near a 20-month high on Tuesday, after Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia's CEO breathed new life into the AI rally and stoked expectations that the recovery would give the Federal Reserve greater scope to raise rates further.

Against the resurgent greenback, the euro languished near an over 18-month low at US$1.0907 after sliding 0.6% overnight, while sterling similarly struggled to bounce from a one-year low and last bought US$1.3037.
The dollar firmed at 104.32 against a basket of currencies, having peaked at 104.53 in the previous session.

Nvidia on Monday reinstated Huang as CEO under pressure from US president Donald Trump, a stunning reversal following his resignation over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged spy for China.
The move reignited the AI euphoria and sparked a blistering rally across equities, with Nvidia adding roughly US$950 billion to its market capitalisation overnight.

"It's really hard to say what Jensen Huang's comeback as the CEO of Nvidia means to the whole AI investment boom, but judging by the equity market movement, investors seem pretty excited about his reinstatement and markets are buying into the whole AI narrative again," said Carol Kong, a currency strategist at Commonwealth Bank of Australia.
"For now, it seems to be a positive for the AI narrative that has been a crucial pillar of the US exceptionalism story that has supported the US dollar."
Traders have now fully priced in a 25-basis-point Fed hike next month and see a slim chance of an outsized 50bp move, up from zero a day earlier, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

The equity market rout over the past week, led by a heavy selloff in technology and chip stocks, had prompted investors to pare back bets on further Fed hikes due to uncertainty over how much more tightening the economy could withstand.

"Our US economists have been flagging that tighter financial conditions and lower equity valuations could limit the Fed's appetite for further tightening, though (Monday's) move is reversing some of that pressure," said Citi markets analyst Preston Pagli.
The yen eased slightly to 159.06 per dollar in the early Asian session, while the Aussie was pinned near an 11-month low at $0.6627.
The New Zealand dollar similarly struggled at US$0.5450, not far from Monday's 17-year trough of US$0.5434.

The Aussie has come under immense pressure in recent sessions on the back of a repricing of domestic rate expectations, with markets now fully pricing in a rate cut next August and a total of 50bp worth of easing by the end of 2027.

Analysts at JP Morgan said in a note that short positions in the Australian dollar against the greenback have "accummulated substantially", with bearish positioning reaching "extreme levels in some cases" by their metrics.

"Looking first at options, AUD puts have been outnumbering calls for several months now. Early in this process, it seemed reasonable to assume that this might simply be macro hedging, rather than actual outright directional positioning. But the flows have probably migrated to the latter of late," they said.

430a02836ea3dd8d: PETALING JAYA: Nazri Aziz menggesa kerajaan mengkaji semula keputusan menamatkan kemasukan tanpa visa bagi warga India, yang dibimbangi menjejaskan sektor pelancongan dan hubungan dua hala.

Bekas menteri pelancongan itu berkata kerajaan perlu meneliti jumlah sebenar warga India yang menyalahgunakan kemudahan itu untuk bekerja atau tinggal melebihi tempoh dibenarkan sebelum menarik balik pengecualian visa kepada semua pelawat dari negara berkenaan.
“Kerajaan patut mempertimbangkan semula keputusan itu. Kita kena jaga hubungan baik dengan India, lebih-lebih lagi ketika Malaysia mahu menarik lebih ramai pelancong.

“Kalau 100,000 orang tidak pulang, itu memang masalah besar. Kerajaan patut mengambil tindakan. Tetapi kalau jumlahnya kurang daripada 1,000 orang, misalnya, adakah wajar kita menyekat kemudahan kepada semua pelancong India?” katanya dalam temu bual bersama FMT.

Beliau mengulas pengesahan Menteri Dalam Negeri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail bahawa pengecualian visa selama 30 hari bagi warga India akan ditamatkan pada 31 Dis ini bagi membolehkan saringan lebih ketat dilakukan sebelum mereka tiba di Malaysia.

Imigresen turut mengeluarkan notis pada 17 Nov lalu memaklumkan pemegang pasport India perlu mendapatkan visa yang sah untuk memasuki Malaysia mulai 1 Jan 2027. Permohonan boleh dibuat melalui portal MyVISA bermula 1 Dis ini.
Bagaimanapun, Suruhanjaya Tinggi Malaysia di New Delhi dilaporkan berkata pengecualian itu dijadualkan tamat pada 31 Dis, namun kemungkinan untuk melanjutkannya masih terbuka.

Terdahulu, pada 22 Sept, Suruhanjaya Tinggi India di Kuala Lumpur memberi amaran mengenai peningkatan warga India yang menyalahgunakan kemudahan tanpa visa untuk mencari pekerjaan, termasuk mereka yang diperdaya ejen menawarkan pekerjaan palsu.

Malaysia memperkenalkan kemudahan itu pada Disember 2023 bagi merancakkan semula sektor pelancongan selepas pandemik Covid-19, dengan warga India dibenarkan berada di negara ini sehingga 30 hari tanpa visa.

Nazri yang juga bekas duta besar Malaysia ke Amerika Syarikat turut mengingatkan India pasaran pelancongan penting bagi Malaysia, dengan ketibaan pelawat dari negara itu meningkat 14.6% kepada 1.56 juta orang pada 2025, berbanding 1.36 juta pada tahun sebelumnya, menurut Tourism Malaysia.
Katanya, penamatan pengecualian visa juga berisiko menyinggung perasaan rakyat India, terutama apabila pelawat dari negara lain masih menikmati kelonggaran sama.
Beliau bimbang keadaan itu boleh menjejaskan hubungan diplomatik kedua-dua negara, malah mendorong pelancong India memboikot Malaysia.
"Jangan kerana dua atau tiga orang melakukan kesalahan, kita menghukum seluruh kelompok. Bak kata orang, kalau hendak menangkap nyamuk, tangkaplah nyamuk. Jangan sampai membakar kelambu,” katanya.

0c78b607dc868c26: PETALING JAYA: Jabatan Perdagangan Amerika Syarikat (AS) menyenaraihitamkan tiga syarikat Malaysia susulan kebimbangan ia mungkin terbabit dalam penyaluran peralatan pengkomputeran canggih kepada pengguna yang tidak dibenarkan.

3d450211450bcc10: ISTANBUL: A global coalition of more than 155 child safety organisations and experts called on Amazon and eBay on Monday to immediately stop selling toys equipped with artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots over concerns about risks to children's safety and development, Anadolu Ajansi reported.

In an open letter to Amazon CEO Andy Jassy and eBay CEO Jamie Iannone, the coalition urged the retailers to suspend sales of toys containing generative AI chatbots marketed to children under 16 until independent testing establishes their safety.
The coalition, which includes Fairplay, Alliance 4 Children and The Anxious Generation Movement, also called on the companies to warn customers who have already purchased such toys and offer refunds.
The letter said more than 50 AI toys were recently found on Amazon's US marketplace, while 28 were identified on its UK platform in late October.

Some products were marketed to children as young as three despite connecting to general-purpose chatbots intended for older users, while others advertised features such as voice cloning and tracking children's emotional development.
The coalition cited tests in which AI toys gave inappropriate sexual responses and instructions involving matches and knives, while also raising concerns about privacy violations.
It also warned that children could develop unhealthy emotional attachments to AI companions, with their long-term effects on development and mental health remaining unknown.
"These products should be shown to be safe before they reach children, not withdrawn one at a time after harm is found," the coalition said.
"Retailers have been pulling AI toys from their shelves one by one when they are called out, but it's not enough," Fairplay's Young Children Thrive Offline Programme Director Rachel Franz said.
The coalition also asked both companies to respond by Christmas so the information could be shared with lawmakers and parents.
The appeal comes as California prepares to introduce a four-year ban on the manufacture and sale of AI companion toys intended for children under 16, beginning Jan 1, 2027.

fbee98991ebdf72a: PETALING JAYA: The US commerce department has placed three Malaysian companies on a trade blacklist over concerns that they could help divert advanced computing hardware to unauthorised users.

The other four companies are Megaspeed International Pte Ltd, Apex Enterprise Solutions (Singapore) Pte Ltd and Swiftdata Pte Ltd in Singapore, and Megaspeed (Thailand) Co Ltd.
BIS cited "the significant risk of these entities being or becoming involved in the diversion of advanced computing commodities to unauthorised end uses or end users".
All seven companies will now need a licence for items subject to US export rules, with applications "reviewed under a presumption of denial".

Speedmatrix is the Malaysian subsidiary of Singapore-based Megaspeed, a cloud computing company and Nvidia partner suspected of helping channel restricted AI chips to China. The company is also linked to an investigation involving alleged espionage related to Nvidia.
The investment, trade and industry ministry (Miti) previously said it never approved any applications from Megaspeed or Speedmatrix, and that Speedmatrix was a tenant at data centres in Malaysia.

Miti also said importing AI chips into Malaysia does not currently require a permit or licence. However, since July last year, companies have needed a permit to export, re-export or move high-performance US-made AI chips through Malaysia.

09b764c1e0bda139: KUALA LUMPUR: Axiata Group Bhd's proposed restructuring of its telecommunications infrastructure subsidiary Edotco Group is expected to strengthen its balance sheet and improve its capacity to pay dividends, analysts said.
Gross proceeds of RM2.22 billion from the exercise have been earmarked largely for debt repayment.

CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd said the proposed transactions will reduce Axiata's net debt-to-earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) ratio from 2.57 times as at the second quarter of 2026 to a pro forma 1.67 times.
The firm said the deal allows Axiata to unlock a substantial portion of Edotco's value while retaining its Malaysian tower operations for potential future monetisation.

Affin Hwang Investment Bank Bhd said the six sale and purchase agreements (SPAs) value Edotco at an enterprise value of RM11.8 billion, equivalent to 8.5 times its financial year 2025 (FY25) Ebitda before the adoption of MFRS 16.

The transactions comprise two parts: Khazanah Nasional Bhd acquires a 15.64 per cent stake in Edotco from Axiata for RM659.4 million, while Edotco divests most of its overseas tower operations to a mix of strategic and financial buyers.

Affin Hwang said the six SPAs are structured such that the first four are inter-conditional and must be completed together, while the disposals of the Pakistan and Cambodia operations can proceed independently.
Under the main transactions, Edotco will distribute RM2.47 billion to its existing shareholders through dividends and/or a capital reduction before completion.
Affin Hwang said the distribution would be funded mainly by RM2.07 billion raised from the disposals under SPAs 2 to 4, supplemented by about RM396 million from Edotco's existing balance sheet.
Axiata's 63 per cent share of the distribution amounts to RM1.56 billion.
Together with the RM659.4 million proceeds from the stake sale to Khazanah, this brings Axiata's total gross proceeds to about RM2.22 billion.
Axiata intends to use RM2.04 billion to repay borrowings, with the balance allocated for transaction-related expenses and taxes.

Affin Hwang said the separate disposals of Edotco's Pakistan and Cambodia operations are expected to generate a combined RM692 million, which is also earmarked for debt repayment but excluded from the RM2.22 billion headline proceeds.
Upon completion, Axiata and Khazanah will each hold a 47.355 per cent stake in Edotco, while Kumpulan Wang Persaraan (Diperbadankan) (KWAP) will retain a 5.29 per cent stake.
Edotco will retain its tower operations in Malaysia and Sri Lanka after exiting Bangladesh, the Philippines, Indonesia, Pakistan and Cambodia.

On the financial impact, CIMB Securities said the RM2.04 billion debt repayment would partly offset the expected RM108 million reduction in Edotco's contribution to Axiata's net profit, based on FY25 figures.
It estimated that the resulting post-tax interest savings would amount to RM62 million, assuming a four per cent interest rate.
Axiata also expects to recognise a one-off net gain of RM2.13 billion from the proposed disposals.
On valuation, CIMB Securities said the deal implies an equity value of RM2 billion for Axiata's remaining 47.355 per cent stake in Edotco.

Together with the RM2.22 billion cash proceeds, this translates into a total realised and unrealised equity value of RM4.21 billion for Axiata's previous 63 per cent stake, close to CIMB Securities' estimated value of RM4.34 billion before applying a holding company discount.
CIMB Securities added that the transaction valuation represents a premium to listed tower companies in Indonesia, India and China, which trade at between 2.9 and 7.3 times Ebitda.
The main transactions involving Khazanah and the disposals in Bangladesh, the Philippines and Indonesia are inter-conditional and targeted for completion by the third quarter of 2027.

The Pakistan and Cambodia disposals are independent transactions targeted for completion by the fourth quarter of 2027. The proposals are subject to relevant shareholder and regulatory approvals, where applicable.
Upon completion, Axiata will deconsolidate Edotco from its financial statements.

CIMB Securities maintained its 'Buy' recommendation on Axiata with an unchanged sum-of-parts-based target price of RM2.30, citing the potential benefits of a stronger balance sheet, lower risk premium and improved dividend-paying capacity.
However, it identified delays or termination of the proposed disposals as key downside risks.
