d5d67283f0ec77a9: WASHINGTON: The United States on Monday added Singapore-based Megaspeed International to a trade blacklist that bars it from purchasing advanced chips, after Nvidia chief executive officer Jensen Huang was accused of having an affair with a Megaspeed executive alleged to be a Chinese spy.

The company, along with four affiliates in Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand, was added to the US Commerce Department's Entity List for "acting contrary to the national security or foreign policy interests of the United States", according to a filing in the Federal Register.
Huang, 63, stepped down after reports emerged that he had a relationship with Alice Huang, no relation, a former Megaspeed executive whose company bought billions of dollars' worth of Nvidia chips.
He was reinstated as Nvidia's CEO on Monday morning, after US President Donald Trump repeatedly insisted he should return to lead a company at the centre of the artificial intelligence revolution.
Monday's designation bars Megaspeed from purchasing AI chips and other advanced technology without a US government licence.
The company has been accused of possibly diverting high-end chips and computing power to China, in contravention of strict US export controls.
US intelligence services have reportedly concluded that Alice Huang passed information to Beijing, which has denied the allegations.
Among the seven firms added to the Entity List on Monday were Singapore-based Swiftdata, Megaspeed's holding company, and its Malaysian affiliate, Speedmatrix.

The move comes after the Trump administration announced tighter export controls on AI chips last week, closing a loophole that allowed Chinese companies to access Nvidia's most advanced chips remotely.
bdcb2ae34ca01922: KUALA LUMPUR: A silver Perodua Bezza was left stranded after its front passenger-side tyre plunged into a massive pothole, leaving its rear wheel suspended in the air, along a road in Plentong, Johor.
The incident was captured in a viral video circulating on Threads, showing the car tilted forward with its front wheel lodged deep inside the cavity.
The video, posted by a Threads user @alysra, has attracted much attention as the pothole is both deep and wide.
Several commenters also alleged that the Bezza was not the first vehicle to be affected, claiming that a motorcycle and another car had ended up in the pothole.
The incident prompted an outpouring of frustration, with some questioning why no action had been taken to repair the damaged road.
One commenter suggested that a burst underground water pipe could have caused the road to collapse.
Another questioned the whereabouts of the local elected representative and the Permas village head.
A social media user also questioned the authorities' response, claiming that the damage had been there for some time.
Another expressed concern over the potential danger to other road users.
Another social media user suggested that owners of the affected vehicles consider taking legal action against the local council and the authority responsible for maintaining the road.
d72fc07dea2532a0: Hari itu Ahmad Maslan berpantun di Dewan Rakyat. Selain terkenal dengan resipi nasi gorengnya, Timbalan menteri kerja raya itu memang gemar berpantun. Tapi, bukan tentang kenapa dan apa sebab beliau berpantun yang ingin saya ceritakan. Tolak ke tepi bab politik, saya rasa ada sesuatu yang wajar kita hargai daripada kegemaran beliau itu. Bagi saya pantun perlu diangkat sebagai pusaka negara dan mesti diajar dengan serius di sekolah ketika kita mencari formula lain dalam usaha menggalakkan pelajar berfikir secara kritis dan kreatif.

Pantun mampu mengasah kemahiran tersebut. Hari ini tak ramai orang mampu berpantun secara spontan. Kalau diberikan pen dan kertas serta masa setengah jam, mungkin ramai yang boleh menghasilkan pantun empat kerat. Itupun pantun yang asal boleh sajalah! Bukan pantun yang betul-betul bermutu tinggi. Tetapi bagaimana jika kita perlu melakukannya dalam masa beberapa saat atau membalas pantun secara spontan? Saya percaya kita memang gagal. Di situlah menariknya pantun sebagai penajam akal.

Kita selalu membicarakan pantun sebagai warisan kesusasteraan Melayu. Tetapi jarang sekali kita membicarakannya dari sudut keupayaan kognitif manusia. Bagi saya, pantun bukan sekadar permainan bahasa, tetapi juga suatu bentuk latihan ketangkasan berfikir. Bayangkan apa yang berlaku dalam kepala seseorang ketika mencipta pantun secara spontan. Kita perlu memikirkan perkara yang hendak disampaikan, mencari perkataan yang sesuai, menyusun ayat, memadankan rima serta membina pembayang. Semua itu dilakukan hampir serentak. Belum lagi kalau pantun itu perlu dijawab apabila ada yang menjualnya.

Otak perlu bekerja untuk memahami maksud yang disampaikan oleh orang lain, merumuskan jawapan dan menterjemahkan jawapan itu dalam bentuk puisi yang mempunyai peraturan tertentu. Ini bukan mudah. Cuma, selama ini kita lihat pantun seolah-olah dipermainkan dan dijadikan bahan lawak sahaja dalam rancangan hiburan atau persembahan komedi. Kita kena serius sekali-sekala.

Dalam bidang pendidikan, kita sering bercakap tentang pemikiran kritis. Kita mahu anak-anak kita mempunyai kemampuan menganalisis, mentafsir, membuat perkaitan dan menyelesaikan masalah secara kreatif. Menariknya, sebahagian daripada kemahiran berfikir itu sudah lama dilatih oleh nenek moyang kita melalui suatu kegiatan yang hari ini sering kita anggap sekadar hiburan.

Bukanlah bermaksud syarat hendak berpantun mestilah mempunyai pemikiran kritis yang tinggi. Tetapi proses mencipta pantun itu sendiri memerlukan beberapa kemahiran mental yang amat berguna dalam membentuk pemikiran seseorang. Pantun juga ada tingkatannya. Ada pantun yang mudah, sekadar memadankan bunyi di hujung baris. Ada pula pantun yang pembayangnya mempunyai hubungan makna dengan maksud yang hendak disampaikan. Lebih tinggi lagi apabila pencipta pantun menggunakan perlambangan alam untuk menyampaikan falsafah kehidupan. Contohnya pantun ini:-
Yang kurik itu kundi, Yang merah itu saga; Yang baik itu budi, Yang indah itu bahasa.

Betapa ekonomisnya penggunaan bahasa dalam menyampaikan suatu pemikiran. Tak perlu panjang berjela, empat baris sahaja sudah cukup untuk membicarakan nilai kemanusiaan. Orang Melayu dahulu memerhatikan alam. Mereka melihat tumbuh-tumbuhan, haiwan, sungai, laut dan perubahan cuaca. Daripada pemerhatian itu, mereka membina perlambangan dan menghubungkannya dengan kehidupan manusia. Ini bukan sekadar persoalan penguasaan bahasa. Ini juga persoalan keupayaan membuat perkaitan antara dua perkara yang pada zahirnya kelihatan tidak mempunyai hubungan. Kemampuan membuat perkaitan inilah yang dimaksudkan sebagai salah satu ciri pemikiran kreatif.

Menteri pendidikan patut beri perhatian yang serius akan kemahiran yang sudah lama kita miliki ini. Pantun bukan sekadar diajar sebagai salah satu bentuk puisi tradisional dalam mata pelajaran bahasa Melayu semata-mata tetapi dijadikan kegiatan yang melatih anak-anak berfikir secara spontan. Adakan sesi jual beli pantun di dalam kelas. Seorang pelajar mengemukakan persoalan dalam bentuk pantun dan seorang lagi menjawabnya juga dalam bentuk pantun. Biarkan mereka belajar sambil berseronok walaupun pada permulaannya mungkin mutu pantun masih rendah. Lama-kelamaan sudah tentu pelajar akan jadi mahir serta tangkas seperti pantun lama ini:
Limau purut lebat di pangkal, Batang mengkudu condong uratnya; Hujan ribut dapat ditangkal, Hati yang rindu apa ubatnya?

Perhatikan kehalusannya. Jika anak-anak kita mampu mencipta pantun sebegini bermakna mereka telah memahami falsafah hubungan perasaan manusia dengan fenomena alam. Hujan ribut yang dahsyat sekalipun masih dianggap mampu ditangkal, tetapi kerinduan yang tidak kelihatan itu belum tentu mampu diubati.

Bayangkan juga jika seorang guru sains meminta anak muridnya menerangkan sesuatu konsep sains melalui pantun. Sudahlah perlu memahami konsep itu, mereka perlu pula memikirkan cara menyampaikannya dalam empat baris. Tentulah ada yang secara sinis mempersoalkan mengapa perlu menyusahkan diri sedangkan penerangan biasa lebih mudah. Inilah yang saya maksudkan sejak awal lagi ia bertujuan untuk mencabar kemampuan minda. Contoh lucunya ialah mamat-mamat sado yang mengangkat besi di gimnasium pun boleh kita tanyakan soalan yang sama. Mengapa bersusah payah mengangkat besi berat sebab lepas itu letak semula besi tersebut di tempat asalnya. Tapi kita segera faham yang dia sedang melatih ototnya, manakala orang yang berpantun pula sedang melatih akalnya.

Dalam zaman kecerdasan buatan hari ini, kita boleh meminta komputer menghasilkan puluhan pantun dalam beberapa saat. Tetapi tujuan mengajar anak-anak berpantun bukanlah semata-mata untuk mendapatkan pantun yang indah. Yang lebih penting ialah proses mental yang dilalui untuk menghasilkan pantun tersebut. Kita tidak mahu sekadar melahirkan generasi yang tahu mendapatkan jawapan. Kita juga mahu melahirkan generasi yang tahu bagaimana hendak berfikir untuk mendapatkan jawapan. Bertuahnya kita ialah kita sudah ada kaedah yang praktikal dalam hal ini tetapi kita kesampingkannya. Orang tua kita dulu apabila berpantun macam, GhatGpt. Prompt saja terus keluar jawapan.

Satu lagi keistimewaan pantun ialah kemampuannya menyampaikan teguran secara halus. Orang boleh berselisih pendapat, menyindir, menegur, malah berbahas tanpa semestinya menggunakan bahasa yang kasar. Dalam zaman manusia begitu mudah memaki hamun di media sosial, alangkah menariknya jika mereka perlu berpantun dahulu sebelum mahu bergaduh. Sekurang-kurangnya ada tapisan sedikit sebelum menghina orang. Kedengaran mungkin lucu, tapi kita lihatlah hari ini berapa ramai mengalami kemurungan akibat dimaki hamun di media sosial. Barangkali ada yang akan membatalkan hasrat untuk bergaduh kerana terlalu sibuk mencari pembayang. Lihatlah ketika Ahmad Maslan berpantun. Bunyinya tenang sahaja tetapi 'makan dalam'. Berbanding beberapa Ahli Parlimen yang gemar menjerit dan bertempik sehingga penyokong sendiri pun naik malu.

Kita patut berbangga dengan warisan budaya kita. Namun, kebanggaan itu tidak seharusnya terhenti pada usaha memelihara bentuknya semata-mata. Kita juga harus menggali kebijaksanaan di sebalik penciptaannya dan mencari bagaimana ia boleh dimanfaatkan dalam kehidupan moden. Pantun bukan sekadar khazanah bahasa. Ia juga khazanah pemikiran. Nenek moyang kita bukan sahaja mewariskan keindahan berbahasa, malah suatu kaedah untuk melatih ketangkasan akal.

Kalau kita sendiri kurang menghargai keistimewaan pantun, tahukah kita bahawa hampir dua abad dahulu sasterawan Perancis sudah tertarik dengannya? Pada tahun 1829, Victor Hugo, pengarang Les Misérables, memperkenalkan pantun berkait Melayu menerusi antologi puisinya, Les Orientales. Bentuk puisi ini kemudian diadaptasi oleh penyair Perancis sehingga dikenali sebagai pantoum.

Bayangkan, ketika orang Eropah sedang meneroka keunikan struktur puisi warisan kita, nenek moyang kita sudah menjadikannya sebahagian daripada cara mereka berkomunikasi dalam kehidupan seharian. Sayang sekali jika kita hanya mewarisi pantunnya tetapi tidak mewarisi kecerdasan berfikir yang melahirkan pantun itu. Dan dalam bab ini, saya menghargai kegemaran Ahmad Maslan berpantun. Agak-agak bernas atau tidak cadangan saya agar kemahiran berpantun diajar secara serius di sekolah?
Artikel ini adalah pandangan penulis dan tidak semestinya mewakili FMT.
97bbc033a9e9fa11: A president’s absence and a president’s disqualification are two different things. Malaysia Athletics must establish what its constitution requires when an incumbent becomes ineligible to hold office.
World Athletics has disqualified Karim Ibrahim. He has not appealed against the decision, and the international governing body has not lifted the sanction.

Article 13.2.8 of Malaysia Athletics’ endorsed constitution sets out the consequence. It makes a person ineligible to be nominated, elected, appointed or hold office if he has been disqualified, removed or suspended by Malaysia Athletics, the Olympic Council of Malaysia, the Asian Athletics Association, World Athletics or another local or international sports authority or organisation.
That ineligibility continues until the relevant authority releases the person from the sanction or he succeeds in an appeal.
Karim’s disqualification therefore makes him ineligible to hold office under this provision. Malaysia Athletics must formally record it and address the consequences for the presidency.
The issue now is not the existence of the sanction, but how the association applies its own constitution to the leadership position it has affected.
The deputy president’s authority needs a clear basis
Malaysia Athletics deputy president Wan Hisham Wan Salleh now regards himself as the acting president. But the constitution must provide a sound basis for that position.

Article 12.2.2 allows the deputy president to chair Malaysia Athletics meetings when the president is absent. It also allows him to assume the president’s rights and duties at those meetings, as designated by the president.
The clause deals with the president’s absence. It does not expressly state that the deputy president automatically becomes acting president when the incumbent is disqualified from holding office.
Nor does it spell out how the deputy president should assume the full responsibilities of the presidency in those circumstances.
That difference cannot be brushed aside.

A president who is away or unable to attend a meeting may still hold office. Disqualification raises a different issue: the incumbent is no longer eligible to occupy the position under Article 13.2.8.
Wan Hisham’s claim to be acting president therefore needs more than an assumption that the deputy president naturally takes over.
The council must identify the constitutional provision, decision or other valid authority that supports his position.

Article 12.2.2 may provide for the deputy president to perform certain duties during the president’s absence. But the wording supplied does not, by itself, establish an automatic succession process after disqualification.
It also does not expressly give the deputy president a mandate to serve as acting president until the next election.
This is where the executive council must do its work. Article 18.1 gives it sole authority to interpret the association’s constitution and by-laws.
It must examine the relevant provisions together, determine what they require and record its decision.

That interpretive power does not allow the council to create a succession rule that the constitution does not contain. It must apply the written provisions, not stretch them to fit an administrative arrangement.
The council should examine Article 12.2.2 alongside Article 13.2.8 and any other clauses dealing with vacancies, removal from office, an acting president or fresh elections.
If another provision sets out the succession process, the council must follow it. If the constitution leaves the position unclear, it should obtain legal advice before deciding how to proceed.
Wan Hisham has said he will brief the executive council at its Nov 29 meeting. He has declined to answer legal and constitutional questions while awaiting legal advice.
The meeting offers the council a timely opportunity to consider the disqualification, clarify the authority under which the association is operating and decide the next steps.
It should leave no doubt about who holds the presidency, what powers that person may exercise and which constitutional provisions support the arrangement.
Other decisions need scrutiny, not sweeping conclusions
The council must also consider whether Karim’s disqualification affects decisions and appointments made during his time in office.
It should not assume that every decision made under his leadership is now invalid. Equally, it should not treat every appointment as beyond question.
Each case requires a review of the relevant eligibility rules, appointment process and circumstances.

The same care applies to the annual general meeting and the election of office-bearers. Karim’s disqualification does not, by itself, invalidate the entire meeting or the positions of everyone elected.
Any challenge must rest on the relevant constitutional provisions and the facts surrounding the election.
Members may also ask whether they can table a motion of no confidence in the current leadership.
The constitution’s provisions on notice, meetings, voting and removal must determine whether they can do so and what effect such a motion would have.
A vote of no confidence does not necessarily remove an office-bearer unless the rules provide for it.
The council should answer these questions by referring to the constitution, not through informal assurances or political agreement.
Members need to know which rules apply and how the association intends to enforce them.
Malaysia Athletics cannot afford further uncertainty over who has authority to lead it and where that authority comes from.
The association must record Karim’s disqualification, establish the status of the presidency and identify the proper process for filling the position.
It must also clarify the deputy president’s powers while that process unfolds.

If the constitution requires an election, the association should follow the prescribed procedure. If it provides another route, the council should explain and apply it. Either way, members must be able to trace the decision to a clear constitutional provision.

This is not a contest between Karim and Wan Hisham, or an opportunity for one faction to gain an advantage over another. It is a test of whether Malaysia Athletics can govern by rules rather than assumptions.
The executive council has the authority to interpret the constitution. It also has a duty to apply it fairly, consistently and transparently.
A constitution cannot be stretched to suit the people who happen to hold office. It exists to govern them, especially when leadership is in dispute. The Nov 29 meeting should make that clear.
The views expressed are those of the writer and do not necessarily reflect those of FMT.
a7aa48776785e95e: KUALA LUMPUR: Ever played a racing video game and wished you could literally jump right into the action?
Imagine speeding around a racetrack, collecting power-ups, dodging obstacles and launching attacks on your opponents in a frenzied bid to rack up the highest score.
Well, thanks to BattleKart, you can now turn those virtual racing fantasies into reality.

Combining the thrills of go-karting with the colourful chaos of arcade gaming, this new attraction transforms a traditional racing experience into an interactive adventure. Think “Mario Kart” brought to life, only without the pesky blue shells!

Opening this month at Longhaus KL in Jalan Chan Sow Lin here, BattleKart offers players the chance to get behind the wheel of an electric go-kart and compete against each other in a series of exciting games.
First launched in Belgium in 2015, BattleKart is the brainchild of engineer Sébastien Millecam, who conceptualised the game while in university.
Since then, the attraction has expanded internationally, with over 50 outlets across Europe, Australia, the Middle East and North America. KL marks its Southeast Asian debut.

Instead of racing around a track, BattleKart players navigate a colourful virtual environment projected onto its arena floor, complete with obstacles, power-ups and other interactive elements. Its karts are equipped with an anti-collision system designed to minimise the risk of accidents.
Using a combination of projection technology and sensors, players interact with the digital world around them, turning the entire arena into a giant video game.
The result is an entertaining blend of physical movement and digital gameplay, where quick reflexes, clever tactics and a little luck can make all the difference between victory and defeat.
To enjoy a BattleKart experience, simply register, hop into a kart and get ready for some high-octane fun!
The vehicles are relatively easy to operate and manoeuvre, and there’s no denying the exhilaration of zipping around the arena taking sharp corners at high speed.

Of course, much of the fun comes from competing against friends, whether it's overtaking a rival just in the nick of time or launching a well-timed attack that sends them tumbling down the leaderboard.

Anyone with a basic understanding of driving will get the hang of things quickly. And while experienced drivers may have an advantage, you certainly don’t need the skills of Lewis Hamilton or Sebastian Vettel to enjoy yourself.
There are seven game modes, each presenting its own thrills and challenges.
The most straightforward is BattleRace, where players race around a virtual circuit, collecting power-ups and launching attacks at their opponents to achieve the highest score.
Those looking for something different can try BattleColor, which challenges teams to claim as much of the arena floor as possible by driving over coloured tiles.
Particularly enjoyable is BattleSnake, a twist on the classic mobile game where players collect virtual fruit to grow a “snake” trailing behind their kart while avoiding obstacles and rival players.
Other game options are BattlePool, BattleFoot, BattleVirus, and BattleWanted.

Each BattleKart session lasts approximately 15 minutes, including the time needed to board and leave the karts. Between two and 10 players can participate in a session, making it suitable for outings with friends, family members or colleagues.
Players must be at least 1.45m tall to participate.
Anyone feeling peckish after their racing adventures can visit Slim Chickens, an American fast-casual restaurant located within the same venue.

The restaurant specialises in chicken tenders and wings, served with its signature sauces. You can’t go wrong with classics like ranch, Korean BBQ and honey mustard, while the more adventurous might enjoy the sweet, fiery kick of mango habanero or the zesty tang of sriracha mayo.

All in alll, BattleKart offers an interesting alternative to the usual indoor entertainment options. Whether you’re a seasoned gamer, an aspiring racing driver or simply someone looking for a different way to spend an afternoon, there’s plenty here to get your adrenaline pumping.
Just remember: in BattleKart, being the fastest driver doesn't necessarily guarantee victory. Sometimes, just one well-aimed rocket can ruin a winning streak!
BattleKart Kuala Lumpur Lot G02, Longhaus KL, No. 1, Jalan Chan Sow Lin, 55200 Kuala Lumpur
Opening hours: 10am–midnight daily
For more information, visit BattleKart KL’s website.
d28d21388ed9e9aa: SIBU: The merger of Parti Sarawak Bersatu (PSB) into the Progressive Democratic Party (PDP) came with no additional terms or conditions, PDP president Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing said, following Datuk Seri Wong Soon Koh's resignation from the party.
Tiong said Clause 3 of the Memorandum of Understanding signed by the two parties made clear that neither party was bound by any additional terms or conditions.
He said both parties had agreed to the clause, rejecting Wong's assertion that the original purpose of joining PDP had not been fulfilled.

"It is therefore unreasonable to claim that 'the original purpose of joining PDP has not been fulfilled' simply because personal political interests were not met," he said in a Facebook post last night.
Tiong said PDP had welcomed former PSB members to strengthen political stability and unity within Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS).

Wong, the incumbent Bawang Assan assemblyman, announced his resignation from PDP on Monday, saying the party's current political direction had deviated from the original purpose and expectations that prompted him to join.
The incumbent Engkilili assemblyman, Dr Johnichal Rayong Ngipa, has also left the party.
On April 6, 2024, Tiong announced that Wong and two senior leaders of the now-dissolved PSB had taken up top positions in PDP.
f8e7aa9d464ad337: JAKARTA: Indonesian authorities charged a former police chief and five other people with treason on Monday, a top detective said, in a probe that has uncovered wiretapping of President Prabowo Subianto's telephone.
Four of them, who are current or former police officials, have already been charged this month for their alleged involvement in spying on Prabowo and other high-profile individuals.
One of those allegedly involved has been identified as Listyo Sigit Prabowo, the former police chief who was fired from his post following the investigation.

The national police's top detective, Asep Safrudin, told reporters on Monday that investigators had gathered sufficient evidence to charge the four as well as two other individuals – identified by their initials LSP, SU, EH, ASN, TK and II – with treason.
"The suspects allegedly conspired, prepared and initiated the implementation of treason... by weakening public trust in the government of President Prabowo Subianto," Asep said.
The full extent of the plot that investigators accuse the six of leading, or their alleged objectives, were not immediately clear.
Under Indonesia's criminal code, the maximum penalty for treason against the president is death by firing squad.
Government officials and politicians, journalists, NGO representatives and business people were also targeted in the alleged wiretap.
Asep said police had seized evidence including phones, laptops and cash.
LSP, who media reports identified as Listyo, allegedly ordered and received surveillance reports from others involved in the plot, Asep said.
Presidential spokesman Prasetyo Hadi said this month that Listyo may have committed 'treason' through his alleged involvement in the scandal.
Prabowo, who took office in 2024, has come under increasing pressure over his government's handling of the economy and response to destructive wildfires.
Students and others have mounted large protests against him in recent weeks, also denouncing what they perceive as growing authoritarianism and rampant corruption.
7938a19f89254d69: SIBU: The merger of Parti Sarawak Bersatu (PSB) with the Progressive Democratic Party (PDP) came with no additional terms or conditions, PDP president Tiong King Sing said following Wong Soon Koh’s resignation from the party.
Tiong cited Clause 3 of the memorandum of understanding signed by the parties, which states: "There are no other terms and conditions binding upon either party."
He said both parties agreed to the clause, rejecting Wong’s assertion that the original purpose of joining PDP had not been fulfilled.

"It is therefore unreasonable to claim that 'the original purpose of joining PDP has not been fulfilled' simply because personal political interests were not met," he said in a Facebook post last night.
Tiong also said PDP welcomed former PSB members to strengthen political stability and unity in Gabungan Parti Sarawak.

Wong, the incumbent Bawang Assan assemblyman, announced his resignation from PDP yesterday, saying the party's political direction had deviated from the original purpose and expectations that prompted him to join the party.
The incumbent Engkilili assemblyman, Johnichal Rayong Ngipa, also left the party.
On April 6, 2024, Tiong announced that Wong and two senior leaders of the now-dissolved PSB had taken up top positions in PDP.
acf068b010b00bb8: TOKYO: Japanese and South Korean stocks surged in early trade on Tuesday, tracking strong gains on Wall Street after the shock reinstatement of Nvidia chief executive officer Jensen Huang.
At around 0030 GMT, the Nikkei 225 was up 3.88 per cent at 58,623.73 points, while South Korea's benchmark Kospi index rose 6.01 per cent to 4,991.76 points.
Shares in artificial intelligence (AI) chip giant Nvidia rocketed more than 30 per cent higher on Monday following Huang's return, extending a rebound after last week's rout.
The tech-focused Nasdaq Composite Index gained 6.5 per cent.
Online brokerage Monex said Tokyo was expected to open higher following the strong rally in the US.
"With the decision for Huang to return as Nvidia's CEO, buying spread across a wide range of stocks in the US... and all three major US indices rose," it said.
"The market will likely remain focused on developments surrounding him," it added.
1c4390d2dda39f27: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's recent invitation to the head of Myanmar's junta and efforts to address race, religion and royalty (3R) issues are key matters to be raised at the Dewan Rakyat sitting today.

According to the Order Paper on Parliament's official website, Hassan Abdul Karim (PH-Pasir Gudang) will ask the Prime Minister during Ministers' Question Time (MQT) whether Malaysia regrets inviting the head of Myanmar's junta to the country.
This is in relation to the International Criminal Court's (ICC) ruling on Nov 19 regarding the killing of thousands of Rohingya civilians by Myanmar security forces.

Datuk Rosol Wahid (PN-Hulu Terengganu) will ask the Prime Minister to state the government's position on measures to ensure 3R issues, especially those involving religion, are not politicised or raised irresponsibly to cause public unease.

During the oral question-and-answer session, Datuk Dr Ahmad Marzuk Shaary (PN-Pengkalan Chepa) will ask the Defence Minister to explain the priority given to locally developed defence technologies and systems in procurement by the Ministry of Defence (Mindef) and Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF).

The technologies highlighted include radars, sensors, surveillance systems, autonomous systems and electronic warfare. These align with defence self-reliance aspirations under the National Defence Industry Policy (DIPN).

Mohd Kurniawan Naim Moktar (BN-Kinabatangan) will ask the Digital Minister to state the government's position on the risk of children developing emotional dependency on artificial intelligence (AI) companions.
The Dewan Rakyat is scheduled to resume the committee-stage debate on the Supply (Budget) Bill 2027 after the question-and-answer session.
According to the Dewan Rakyat calendar, the debate is scheduled to run until Nov 26.
666832f1fda22c65: SINGAPORE: Singapore's gross domestic product (GDP) growth outlook for the rest of 2026 remains firm, a trade ministry official said on Tuesday.

Strong momentum in global artificial intelligence (AI) investment is expected to continue for the rest of the year, although the pace of growth in new AI investment is expected to moderate from its high in 2026, said Ministry of Trade and Industry permanent secretary Beh Swan Gin.
Singapore upgraded its 2026 economic growth forecast to around 6.0 per cent on Tuesday after posting third-quarter expansion of 6.1 per cent from a year earlier, government data showed.
The July to September growth was higher than the official advance estimate of 5.4 per cent and above the 5.6 per cent expected in a Reuters poll of economists.
On a quarter-on-quarter, seasonally adjusted basis, GDP expanded by 1.5 per cent in the July to September period, compared with the advance estimate of 1.1 per cent growth.
The Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) now expects GDP growth in 2027 to come in at between 2.5 per cent and 4.5 per cent.

"Although elevated energy prices have contributed to global inflationary pressures and tighter monetary policy in several economies, on balance, MTI's assessment is that Singapore's external demand outlook for the year has improved compared with the assessment in August," the ministry said.
In a separate statement, Enterprise Singapore upgraded its non-oil domestic exports growth forecast for 2026 to between 30 per cent and 32 per cent, from 14 per cent to 16 per cent previously.
This was driven primarily by AI-related growth in electronics and specialised machinery, as well as support from lumpy exports of ships' and boats' structures.

Singapore had in August upgraded its growth forecast for this year to between 4.5 per cent and 5.5 per cent, from the previous range of 2.0 per cent to 4.0 per cent, saying the impact of the Middle East war had been less severe than initially feared, while the global AI investment boom had been stronger than expected.
Singapore's key consumer price gauge rose 1.5 per cent in October from a year earlier.
Last month, the central bank kept its monetary settings unchanged in a move that surprised analysts, with inflation risks expected to ease slightly as the AI boom and supply constraints moderate.
be4c579e4823b209: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened mostly higher against major currencies but was little changed against the US dollar on Tuesday, as expectations of multiple US Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hikes next year continued to support the greenback.
At 8am, the local currency stood at 4.1205/4.1260 against the US dollar, virtually unchanged from Monday’s close of 4.1205/4.1250.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Afzanizam Rashid said the US Dollar Index (DXY) was hovering around 104 points amid the Fed’s hawkish stance.

He said New York Fed president John Williams had indicated in a speech that the central bank needed to bring inflation down to its two per cent target, which he expected could be achieved sometime in 2028.
Afzanizam said the two-year US Treasury yield had risen by five basis points to 4.69%, with shorter-dated securities typically reflecting monetary policy expectations.
"This gives the impression that there could be multiple interest rate hikes next year.
"As such, the ringgit is expected to remain under pressure against the US dollar in the near term," he added.

The ringgit strengthened against the euro to 4.4946/4.5006 from 4.5214/4.5264 at Monday’s close and against the British pound to 5.3707/5.3778 from 5.4032/5.4091. However, it weakened against the Japanese yen to 2.5913/2.5950 from 2.5896/2.5925.
Against other Asean currencies, the ringgit traded mixed.
It appreciated against the Singapore dollar to 3.1905/3.1955 from 3.1949/3.1987 but slipped against the Thai baht to 12.1205/12.1460 from 12.1091/12.1274.
The local note was unchanged against the Indonesian rupiah at 226.3/226.7 and the Philippine peso at 6.45/6.46.
7536fb8137d088f9: KUALA LUMPUR: One of the dangers of diabetic eye disease, or diabetic retinopathy, is that damage can begin before a person notices anything is wrong.

Diabetic retinopathy affects blood vessels in the retina and can eventually lead to vision loss or blindness. In its early stages, it could cause no symptoms at all, making regular screening especially important for those with diabetes.

Malaysia is now looking to artificial intelligence to help identify those changes earlier. According to MyDigital Corporation, health ministry modelling suggests AI-assisted diabetic eye screening could prevent cases of blindness while also reducing the longer-term costs of treatment and care.

Preventing 67 cases of blindness, it said, would be enough to outweigh the combined cost of cameras, AI software and staff time used to run the programme. The estimated savings could reach between RM10 million and RM20 million.

The technology works by analysing retinal images and flagging abnormalities that may need further assessment. Rather than replacing doctors, the aim is to help identify patients who should be referred for closer examination or treatment.

That matters because diabetic retinopathy becomes more difficult to manage once significant damage has occurred. Early diagnosis can give patients a better chance of protecting their sight before symptoms become obvious.

Diabetic eye screening is only one area in which AI is being introduced into Malaysian healthcare. By the end of the year, 902 health clinics nationwide are targeted to offer AI-assisted screening for lung disease.

Data from the National Lung Health Registry recorded 3,053 chest X-rays analysed using AI this year, with 1,429 abnormalities identified through AI analysis. The tech is also being used in breast-cancer testing and radiotherapy.

At a facility in Subang Jaya, computational pathology technology is helping pathologists assess HER2 expression in breast-cancer tissue samples. A multinational study found AI assistance increased agreement between pathologists while reducing the time needed to review cases.
Meanwhile, a hospital in Kuala Lumpur has introduced an AI-powered adaptive radiotherapy system that allows treatment plans to be adjusted according to a patient's anatomy on the day of treatment.
For people living with diabetes, the eye-screening application may be among the easiest to understand: find damage earlier, refer patients sooner, and potentially prevent avoidable sight loss.
bf5d8a15cdf7a3cc: CAIRO: An Israeli airstrike killed at least three Palestinians on Tuesday near a police outpost in Khan Younis in the southern Gaza Strip, local health officials said.
Five other people were wounded in the attack, medics added. There was no immediate comment from the Israeli military on the attack.
An October 2025 US-backed ceasefire halted major fighting in the shattered territory, but has not stopped Israeli attacks on Gaza or secured Hamas' disarmament.
At least 1,600 Palestinians and five Israeli soldiers have been killed since then, according to respective Palestinian and Israeli tallies.
Israeli troops now control around two-thirds of Gaza, up from more than half at the time of the ceasefire, with Hamas controlling a sliver of territory along Gaza's coast.

Israel's more than two-year-long assault on Gaza has killed tens of thousands, caused a hunger crisis, internally displaced the territory's entire population and led to assessments of genocide by scholars and a United Nations inquiry.
Israel has said its actions were in self-defence after Hamas-led fighters killed 1,200 people and took more than 250 hostages in an October 2023 attack on Israel.
64fd93618e8443c4: NEW YORK: New York Federal Reserve President John Williams said on Monday that persistently high inflation continues to point the US central bank towards tighter monetary policy, while stressing that the pace of future interest rate increases will depend on incoming economic data.

"We must take actions over time that will ensure that we get inflation back to our two per cent goal in a timely manner and on a sustained basis," Williams said in remarks at an event held by the University of Mount Saint Vincent in New York. "There is still work to do to get that done."
Williams said inflation was "too high". He noted that he would continue to assess incoming data to decide what action the central bank should take at its December 8-9 policy meeting.

Williams' comments suggested he favours a rate hike at the upcoming meeting. Beyond that, Williams said the path of monetary policy would depend on the economy's performance. "I don't have in my mind a particular timing," Williams told reporters.

"We're going to have to learn along the way as we get more data," Williams said, while noting that "I'm not excluding options" when it comes to the pace of future actions. "I would not exclude, you know, moving at consecutive meetings at all if that was what was needed."
If the economy showed considerable strength and inflation pressures were not moderating, "you wouldn't just want to wait around" and would instead act by adjusting monetary policy, the official said.
Financial markets broadly expect the Fed to raise its policy rate by a quarter of a percentage point next month from the current 3.75 to 4.00 per cent range, with further increases to come next year.

The Fed last raised rates in September as part of an effort to curb inflation, which has been above its two per cent target for more than five years. Central bank officials worry that, if this situation persists, the public could lose confidence that inflation will return to that level.

In recent weeks, a wide range of Fed officials have pointed to the need for further rate hikes. Some policymakers have said they would like to see increases come gradually to allow the economy to adjust, while Fed Governor Christopher Waller has signalled he could support a more aggressive half-percentage-point increase given the hot price pressure data.

Williams was speaking on the same day as a sharp stock market rally, triggered by chipmaker Nvidia's announcement that it was reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO, after US President Donald Trump urged it to do so.

Investors' reaction highlighted the importance of artificial intelligence companies in driving the markets. Some observers had wondered in recent days whether sharp stock losses might deter the Fed from raising rates.
Williams told reporters he was not surprised by the market's volatility and said that, so far, what had happened had not dimmed his optimism about the future of the economy.
Williams also said in his formal remarks that he expects inflation to end the year at 3.5 per cent and moderate to just above two per cent next year before easing to the target in 2028.

He also noted that risks to inflation continue to be skewed to the upside, adding that energy prices remain elevated among the key drivers of high price pressures, while the outlook on that front remains uncertain.

He added that "although the effects of tariffs, geopolitical conflicts, and the AI surge are showing up in prices of certain categories of goods, there is little evidence of these spilling over significantly into broader and more persistent inflation."
Williams also said the economy was showing strength and resilience and should grow by 2.75 per cent in both 2026 and 2027.
He added that the job market had been showing stability, and the current 4.1 per cent unemployment rate should fall to around four per cent next year.

b776de684ef98e0c: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia and Laos aim to raise bilateral trade to US$100 million by 2028, with rail and port links high on the agenda at bilateral talks on Monday.

Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan and Laos Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Thongsavan Phomvihane discussed ways to ease logistics bottlenecks and expand Malaysian investment in hydropower, mining, agriculture, and logistics.

"Discussions covered rail corridors toward China, dry-port links to Malaysian seaports, a proposed undersea cable, and joint efforts to resolve current logistics bottlenecks," the Foreign Ministry, also known as Wisma Putra, said in a Facebook post.
The ministry said both sides also discussed advancing cross-border green energy cooperation under the Laos-Thailand-Malaysia-Singapore Power Integration Project (LTMS-PIP).
The ministry said both governments are preparing the agenda for the fourth Joint Commission for Bilateral Cooperation (JCBC) meeting, which Laos will host in 2027.
"The focus remains on translating diplomatic engagements into stronger regional networks and tangible outcomes for the mutual benefit of both countries," the statement read.

Meanwhile, in a Facebook post, Mohamad said he and Thongsavan also signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) on diplomatic training cooperation between Malaysia's Institute of Diplomacy and Foreign Relations (IDFR) and Laos' Institute of Foreign Affairs (IFA).
Mohamad also hosted a luncheon in honour of Thongsavan's official visit.
The event featured a cake cutting ceremony in conjunction with the 60th anniversary of the establishment of Malaysia–Laos diplomatic ties.
The six decades of diplomatic relations signifies a bond that is strong and flourishing, based on mutual respect and a commitment to foster deeper cooperation in areas of mutual benefit.
Thongsavan arrived here Sunday for a three-day official visit, as Laos and Malaysia mark 60 years of diplomatic relations.
In 2025, bilateral trade between Malaysia and Laos increased by 157.8 per cent compared with the previous year, reaching RM258.4 million (US$60.7 million).
Malaysia's exports to Laos amounted to RM77.7 million (US$18.2 million), while imports from Laos totalled RM180.7 million (US$42.6 million).
From January to August 2026, bilateral trade increased by 28.7 per cent compared with the same period in 2025, reaching RM225.3 million (US$55.9 million).
Malaysian investments in Laos include the 260-megawatt Don Sahong Hydropower Project in Champasak, Malaysia's largest clean energy investment in the country.
f8360b7a6f0bf078: SINGAPORE: Singapore further raised this year’s growth forecast as the artificial intelligence boom delivers a larger-than-expected lift to the economy, defying the drag from higher oil prices and the recent tech selloff in the stock market.

Gross domestic product is expected to expand “around 6%” this year, the energy, trade, and industry ministry (Meti) said on Tuesday. It’s the third time this year the government has upgraded its growth view, from a modest 1%-3% announced in 2025 to 2%-4% in February and then 4.5%-5.5% estimate in August.

That puts Singapore in a position to notch its best annual performance since 2021, based on Bloomberg data. Bolstering the optimism, GDP grew 6.1% in the third quarter, well beating the government’s advance estimate of 5.4% and the median 5.6% forecast in a Bloomberg survey.

Singapore has been a major beneficiary in the trillion-dollar investment surge in AI technology, with the city-state accounting for 10% of all chips produced globally and 20% of semiconductor manufacturing equipment.

The city-state’s non-oil domestic exports rose almost 46% in the third quarter, with electronics more than doubling, according to separate data from Enterprise Singapore. Shipments to the US, the top destination, were up about 74%.
It also puts the city-state at the frontlines as investors start to reckon with the sustainability of the AI boom heading into 2027.

While the return of Jensen Huang at the helm of Nvidia revived optimism in stock markets on Tuesday, the longer-term outlook is still clouded by concerns over tech industry’s rampant debt-financed spending as well as increased regulation and political scrutiny. Huang’s espionage scandal at Nvidia has also triggered more stringent US chip export rules to nations including Singapore.
For 2026, at least, the AI momentum should continue to carry Singapore. Tech demand will drive growth in manufacturing and wholesale trade, Meti said in a statement.
GDP growth is expected to normalise to 2.5%-4.5% in 2027, though the range is higher than the 1%-3% the Meti has recently set at the start of new years.
e3f789bebf421371: PETALING JAYA: Malaysia is introducing a mobile emergency alert system that will send disaster warnings directly to people in affected areas, similar to systems used in Japan for earthquakes and in the UK for severe weather emergencies.

With a nationwide test scheduled for Nov 29, the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) is urging users to update their mobile phones to their latest operating system versions and check their emergency-alert settings.
FMT explains how the Early Warning System (EWS) will work and what you need to do to get your phone ready.
How alerts will reach you
The EWS will warn people in areas at risk from threats of disasters such as floods, landslides and tsunamis.

It will use cell broadcast technology to send messages simultaneously to all compatible phones within a designated area via 4G and 5G networks, rather than sending individual SMS messages to specific phone numbers.
The warning will appear directly onscreen, accompanied by an alarm sound.
It does not require users to install an app, register for a service or have mobile internet access.
According to MCMC, these broadcasts will not be affected by network congestion that can delay calls and SMS messages, although they still require a functioning mobile network for delivery.
Global Environment Centre’s Kalithasan Kailasam welcomed the system as an important step towards building disaster-resilient communities.
He said a limitation of existing information portals was that users had to actively check them for updates, whereas the EWS would deliver localised warnings directly to people in at-risk areas.
“This will reduce or to some extent eliminate the time gap, allowing people to stay informed and act immediately on their own,” he told FMT.
Get your phones ready
MCMC is advising users to install the latest software updates available for their devices, restart them and enable emergency alerts where applicable.
Its preliminary compatibility guide lists iPhone 11 and newer models running iOS 27.2 or later, Android phones running Android 12 or later, and Huawei phones running EMUI 16 or later.
These requirements remain subject to final technical confirmation, while compatibility will also depend on the device and its support for Malaysia’s alert system.

To receive emergency alerts, a mobile phone must be switched on and connected to a working 4G or 5G network. Phones that are turned off, set to airplane mode, or outside network coverage will not receive the alerts.
Could it make a difference?
Malaysians interviewed by FMT, particularly for those living in disaster-prone areas, welcomed the initiative.

Segar Sundera, 70, said the alerts would help keep the public informed of potential dangers, citing the increasing incidence of flash floods, which can cause major disruptions and damage to homes and vehicles, as an example of why early warning is critical.
Business analyst Gautam Karupiah, 26, who frequently encounters flooded roads on his way home, hopes the warnings will prevent motorists from being caught off guard.
“If they can get it done right and they actually warn you an hour early or half an hour early, it should be very helpful for a lot of people just to plan their trips,” he said.
Policeman Danial Abdul Karim, 30, stressed the importance of being prepared.
“Something like this is very good for Malaysians because it helps us be better prepared for disasters,” he said.
What to do when an alert arrives?

When a message appears, read it carefully, check whether it identifies itself as a test and follow the instructions. For an actual emergency, act on the safety directions given, such as evacuating or taking shelter.
Kalithasan urged the authorities to ensure that people understand exactly what action they must take upon receiving a warning.
“As this is a critical first step, the authorities also need to provide clear guidelines on the next step,” he said.
He urged the authorities to share the GPS locations of evacuation centres, emergency contact numbers and checklists for grab bags and 72-hour emergency kits.
He also called for dedicated local helplines so senior citizens and people with disabilities can request assistance tailored to their needs.
The EWS is intended to complement existing warning channels, including SMS, sirens and broadcast announcements.
The public should continue to follow official warnings and instructions from local authorities, even if no alert is received on their phones.
f1529dd02327d2b3: PETALING JAYA: Malaysia bakal memperkenalkan sistem amaran kecemasan yang menghantar maklumat bencana terus ke telefon bimbit penduduk di kawasan terjejas, sama seperti sistem amaran gempa bumi di Jepun dan cuaca buruk di United Kingdom.

Menjelang ujian di seluruh negara pada 29 Nov, Suruhanjaya Komunikasi dan Multimedia Malaysia (SKMM) menggesa pengguna mengemas kini sistem operasi telefon bimbit kepada versi terkini serta menyemak tetapan amaran kecemasan pada peranti masing-masing.
FMT menjelaskan cara sistem amaran awal (EWS) ini berfungsi dan persediaan yang perlu dilakukan bagi memastikan telefon bimbit dapat menerima amaran berkenaan.
Bagaimana amaran dihantar
EWS akan memberi amaran kepada penduduk di kawasan berisiko dilanda bencana seperti banjir, tanah runtuh dan tsunami.

Sistem itu menggunakan teknologi penyiaran sel (cell broadcast) bagi menghantar amaran secara serentak kepada semua telefon bimbit yang serasi dalam kawasan tertentu menerusi rangkaian 4G dan 5G, berbanding SMS yang dihantar kepada nombor telefon secara individu.
Amaran akan dipaparkan terus pada skrin telefon bersama bunyi penggera.
Pengguna tidak perlu memasang sebarang aplikasi, mendaftar perkhidmatan atau mempunyai akses internet mudah alih untuk menerima amaran berkenaan.

Menurut SKMM, kaedah itu tidak terjejas oleh kesesakan rangkaian yang boleh melambatkan panggilan telefon dan penghantaran SMS. Bagaimanapun, rangkaian mudah alih masih perlu berfungsi bagi membolehkan amaran diterima.

Wakil Global Environment Centre (GEC), Kalithasan Kailasam, menyambut baik pelaksanaan sistem itu yang disifatkannya sebagai langkah penting dalam membina masyarakat lebih bersedia dan berdaya tahan menghadapi bencana.
Beliau berkata, antara kelemahan saluran maklumat sedia ada ialah pengguna perlu menyemak sendiri portal berkaitan untuk mendapatkan perkembangan terkini.
Sebaliknya, EWS akan menghantar amaran terus kepada penduduk di kawasan berisiko tanpa perlu mereka mencari maklumat terlebih dahulu.

"Ini dapat mengurangkan, malah pada tahap tertentu menghapuskan kelewatan penyampaian maklumat supaya orang ramai sentiasa mendapat maklumat terkini dan boleh segera bertindak sendiri," katanya kepada FMT.
Persediaan telefon bimbit

SKMM menasihatkan pengguna memasang kemas kini perisian terkini yang tersedia untuk peranti masing-masing, menghidupkan semula telefon selepas kemas kini dan mengaktifkan fungsi amaran kecemasan jika berkenaan.

Berdasarkan panduan awal keserasian peranti, sistem itu menyokong iPhone 11 dan model lebih baharu yang menggunakan iOS 27.2 atau versi seterusnya, telefon Android dengan Android 12 ke atas serta telefon Huawei yang menggunakan EMUI 16 ke atas.
Bagaimanapun, syarat itu masih tertakluk kepada pengesahan teknikal akhir. Keupayaan menerima amaran juga bergantung pada jenis peranti dan sama ada ia menyokong sistem amaran Malaysia.
Untuk menerima amaran, telefon bimbit mesti dihidupkan dan disambungkan kepada rangkaian 4G atau 5G yang berfungsi.
Telefon yang dimatikan, berada dalam mod kapal terbang atau di luar kawasan liputan rangkaian tidak akan menerima amaran berkenaan.
Sejauh mana sistem ini membantu?
Rakyat yang ditemu bual FMT menyambut baik inisiatif itu, khususnya kerana ia dapat membantu penduduk di kawasan yang sering dilanda bencana.
Segar Sundera, 70, berkata sistem berkenaan dapat memastikan orang ramai mengetahui lebih awal mengenai kemungkinan bahaya yang bakal dihadapi.
Beliau mengambil contoh kejadian banjir kilat yang semakin kerap berlaku sehingga mengganggu aktiviti harian serta menyebabkan kerosakan besar kepada rumah dan kenderaan.
Menurutnya, keadaan itu menunjukkan betapa pentingnya amaran awal bagi mengurangkan kesan bencana.
Penganalisis perniagaan, Gautam Karupiah, 26, yang sering berdepan jalan dinaiki air ketika dalam perjalanan pulang, berharap sistem itu dapat membantu pemandu mengelakkan situasi berbahaya.
"Jika sistem ini berfungsi dengan baik dan amaran dapat diberikan sejam atau setengah jam lebih awal, ia tentu sangat membantu orang ramai merancang perjalanan," katanya.
Sementara itu, anggota polis Danial Abdul Karim, 30, menekankan kepentingan persediaan awal sebelum berlakunya bencana.
"Sistem seperti ini sangat baik untuk rakyat Malaysia kerana ia membantu kita membuat persediaan lebih rapi menghadapi bencana," katanya.
Apa perlu dibuat apabila menerima amaran?
Apabila menerima amaran, pengguna perlu membaca mesej dengan teliti dan memastikan sama ada ia sekadar ujian atau amaran kecemasan sebenar.
Jika berlaku kecemasan, orang ramai perlu mematuhi arahan keselamatan yang diberikan, termasuk berpindah ke kawasan selamat atau mendapatkan perlindungan.
Kalithasan turut menggesa pihak berkuasa memastikan orang ramai benar-benar memahami tindakan yang perlu diambil selepas menerima amaran.
"Oleh sebab ini langkah pertama yang amat penting, pihak berkuasa juga perlu menyediakan panduan jelas mengenai tindakan seterusnya," katanya.

Beliau mencadangkan pihak berkuasa turut berkongsi lokasi GPS pusat pemindahan, nombor telefon kecemasan serta senarai barangan keperluan untuk beg kecemasan dan kit persediaan menghadapi bencana selama 72 jam.
Selain itu, beliau menggesa talian bantuan khusus diwujudkan di peringkat tempatan bagi membolehkan warga emas dan orang kurang upaya (OKU) mendapatkan bantuan mengikut keperluan masing-masing.
EWS diperkenalkan sebagai pelengkap kepada saluran amaran bencana sedia ada, termasuk SMS, siren dan pengumuman menerusi siaran media.
Orang ramai juga diingatkan terus mengikuti amaran rasmi dan mematuhi arahan pihak berkuasa tempatan, walaupun tidak menerima sebarang amaran melalui telefon bimbit.
748611fa0bacbe1b: WASHINGTON: Christopher Raia, the FBI's deputy director, intends to retire in December, the Washington Post reported on Monday, citing three people familiar with the matter, marking the latest departure from the bureau during the Trump administration.
The FBI and the US justice department did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Raia, a longtime FBI career official, was tapped in January to replace right-wing podcaster and former Secret Service agent Dan Bongino, who was regarded as unconventional pick for the role.
Before this role, Raia was assistant director in charge of the New York Field Office and has been with the FBI since 2003, previously serving as a top counterterrorism official.

Major personnel changes have taken place at the FBI during Donald Trump's second term in which political experts have raised concerns over the president's use of federal probes to go after political opponents and critics.

af2379ca2419bb97: The leaders of the great model houses, Anthropic's Dario Amodei and OpenAI's Sam Altman, desperately want the world to believe AI is the skeleton key which will unlock the secrets of the universe.
But if the AI can’t explain what it’s “proven,” are we actually any closer to understanding anything, or have we simply built another black box?

That question is top of mind among mathematicians and computer scientists this week after Anthropic researcher Levent Alpöge claimed to have solved a mathematical conjecture so elusive it's gone unproven for more than 150 years. The fact that this note came out one day after Anthropic's record-setting IPO is a coincidence, we're sure.

In a four-page post to his website, the researcher described how with the help of Claude, he believes he has proven the Riemann Hypothesis, one of seven Millennium problems so complex and so important that the Clay Mathematics Institute has offered a $1 million prize to anyone who is successful in solving them.

The Riemann Hypothesis, conjectured by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in 1859, contends that all nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function – those with a real part between zero and one – have a real part equal to 1/2.

Confused? Don’t worry. We’ve linked to an explainer that goes into more detail here. What's important is that, if the Riemann Hypothesis is right, mathematicians can place tighter bounds on the difference between the actual distribution of prime numbers and mathematical estimates of that distribution.

Researchers have previously attempted to disprove the conjecture through computational brute force, and therein have shown the hypothesis holds to at least 10 trillion zeros. There’s reason to believe that the Riemann Hypothesis is accurate, but the possibility remains that over a sufficiently long series the pattern might diverge. And so, more than 150 years after Riemann published his hypothesis, it has remained just that.
Alpöge’s proof, if it can even be called that, is now the subject of great debate.

The four pages in which Alpöge remarks on the discoveries he and Claude made aren’t exactly a proof, but rather 14 tarballs worth of Lean code totaling roughly 240 MB. Lean is an open source programming language commonly used to help validate mathematical proofs.

The Clay Mathematics Institute, which oversees the seven Millennium Problems, has promoted the Riemann Hypothesis from “unsolved” to “active” status, but it is not yet considered solved. For Clay to consider the problem solved and award the prize, the proposed solution must be published in a qualifying outlet, remain available for scrutiny for at least two years, and receive broad acceptance from the mathematics community.
As it stands, Alpöge describes the 250,000 pages of text generated by the model for its written proof as a “massive unreadable travesty of ‘slop.’”

Not long after Alpöge's remarks and Lean code were published, Stanford mathematician Ravi Vakil released a nearly 1,000-page draft proof by Alessandro Maria Masullo, who earned his PhD at Stanford in 2020. Masullo has reportedly spent more than a decade pursuing the problem.

Frameworks like Lean make mathematics a prime candidate for AI-assisted discovery for many of the same reasons that the technology has proven so successful in software development: code either compiles and runs or it doesn’t.

Code can also be audited and could, with great effort, be deciphered. But a proof written in Lean isn't a mathematical proof in the traditional, human-readable sense. Although its logical validity can be checked by a computer, understanding the reasoning behind it can be another matter. Traditional proofs ideally explain their arguments in a way that other mathematicians can follow. Cantor's Diagonal Argument offers a comparatively accessible example.
While the clock hasn’t even started for the Clay Math Institute, the Lean Focused Research Organization and Mathlib Initiative have already declared the Riemann Hypothesis solved.

“We have full confidence that Alpöge's proof of the Riemann Hypothesis is correct, and we congratulate him on this achievement,” the orgs wrote in a joint statement. “We hereby certify that both the statement and the proof of the Riemann Hypothesis are correct.”
Even if the code ends up being right, if we still don’t know why it’s true, have we really learned anything meaningful?
"At the minute, we don't even know why the theorem is true," Kevin Buzzard, professor of pure mathematics at Imperial College London, said in a recent Al Jazeera interview.
Alpöge’s proof may simply be the product of a black box. To quote the late Arthur C Clarke, “any sufficiently advanced technology is indistinguishable from magic.”
The implications of such a technology aren’t lost on researchers. Months ago, several prominent researchers called for greater scrutiny and oversight regarding the application of AI in mathematics.

“Mathematics produces not only a body of results, but also understanding, clarity, and judgment among the communities of mathematicians who have shaped them, often in the context of their own autonomously guided research,” the Leiden Declaration reads. “This expert knowledge is essential, both to effectively use mathematics, and to continue to articulate new and significant research questions.” ®

541fa1c1b5401002: PETALING JAYA: Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Ahmad Zahid Hamidi’s resistance to extending electoral cooperation between his coalition and Perikatan Nasional (PN) may be a form of leverage in negotiations for seat allocations in the four PN-led states of Kelantan, Terengganu, Kedah and Perlis, says an analyst.
Syaza Shukri of International Islamic University Malaysia said Zahid was drawing a line in the sand for fear that PN, the larger Malay coalition, could encroach on BN's support base.
"I think this is insurance in case things do not work out with PN. Zahid needs to maintain that BN and PN are two different entities," she told FMT.

On Nov 15, a day after BN and PN’s victory in the Melaka election, Zahid said there were no plans to extend their cooperation to the 16th general election (GE16), and that discussions on the matter would take place in due time.
His position differed from that of PAS information chief Ahmad Fadhli Shaari, who urged the coalitions to begin negotiations immediately, particularly on seat allocations and strategies for GE16.
PN chairman Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar said on Nov 19 that both coalitions must be willing to make concessions for political cooperation.

Ahmad Zaharuddin Sani Ahmad Sabri of Global Asia Consulting said there was a difference between winning a state election and winning GE16, and that Umno could not afford to lose its political strength, which could be instrumental in deciding whether it leads the government.
"Zahid's greatest fear may not be losing GE16 to PN – it may be winning GE16 with PN, only to discover that Umno has lost its political dominance," he told FMT.
Will BN or PN take Putrajaya?
Zaharuddin said PN would likely face the same problem as BN if it won GE16: determining who would take the reins at Putrajaya.

He warned that Samsuri should not publicly insist on cooperating with BN, saying this would play into Zahid’s hands. "In politics, appearing desperate can be more damaging than actually being desperate," he added.
Zaharuddin said while Samsuri might be concerned about Zahid’s resistance to cooperation, his concern was not rooted in a fear that PN would not perform well in GE16 without BN.
"Samsuri is not afraid of fighting GE16 without BN. He is afraid of winning enough seats to celebrate, but not having enough seats to govern.
"He has to convince Malaysians that PN can govern a multiracial nation rather than dominate the Malay political heartland," Zaharuddin said.
Syaza said there was ultimately no real cause for concern about Umno’s resistance, as BN would have to begin negotiations with PN if it wanted a fighting chance in GE16.

"By hook or by crook, they are going to have to work out the negotiations and cooperate. If they don’t negotiate and instead return to three-cornered electoral fights, BN will be the biggest loser, as it was in 2022, and PN will continue as the biggest Malay coalition," she said.

In GE15, BN won 30 seats, down from 79 in 2018, while PN won 74 seats in 2022, eight fewer than frontrunner Pakatan Harapan. GE16 must be held by February 2028, unless Parliament is dissolved earlier.

03d140d0eca25160: IPOH: From watching a film under the night sky at Ipoh Padang to catching musical theatre in a café, visitors to Perak's charming capital will soon be able to experience the city as one sprawling cultural stage.
Ipoh Festival 2026 will spread performances, exhibitions, traditional crafts and community activities across the city rather than concentrating them in a single venue.

Held under the theme “Turning the City into a Stage”, the four-week festival will transform cafés, galleries, heritage buildings and public spaces into temporary venues, with a particular focus on encouraging visitors to explore Ipoh Old Town.
Among the highlights is Wayang & Makan di Padang, an outdoor cinema experience at Ipoh Padang, alongside musical theatre performances in selected cafés and traditional craft showcases at Tin Alley.

The Artisan Rhythm Market on Jalan Bandar Timah will bring together local makers and businesses, while the Ipoh Mali Theatre Society will stage a food and arts crawl combining performances with visits to different venues around the city.

Music fans can also expect a separate crawl by Indiescape, while local ensembles including the Perak Society of Performing Arts, Perak Wind Orchestra and Choir, Kinta Valley Wind Orchestra and Kumpulan Selendang Perak are among those taking part.
For visitors unsure where to begin, 22 Hale Street Heritage Gallery will serve as the festival information centre and a starting point for exploring the town's history, food and cultural heritage.

Visual arts will also feature prominently. Senitra Studio Gallery will present “Rootbound: Origin and Boundless Expression”, while the contemporary exhibition “Yellow” will bring together works by The Ipoh Fine Arts Class and Perak Contemporary Artists.
Other activities throughout the four weekends include workshops, dance and music performances, documentary screenings and cultural showcases by local creative groups.

Organisers say the idea is not simply to stage a series of events but to encourage residents and visitors to experience familiar parts of Ipoh differently, while giving local artists, cultural organisations and businesses a shared platform.

The festival also aims to connect the city’s heritage with its contemporary creative scene, particularly for younger residents who may pass familiar buildings and streets without knowing much about the stories behind them.
Inspired in part by established events such as George Town Festival and Urbanscapes, organisers hope Ipoh Festival will eventually become a signature annual event for the city.
Admission to most programmes is free, although a small number of activities require prior registration.
Ipoh Festival runs from Nov 27-Dec 19. Find out more and keep updated via Instagram and Facebook.

Pasca PRN Melaka yang sekali lagi menyaksikan Barisan Nasional (BN) dan Perikatan Nasional (PN) menguasai kerusi majoriti Melayu, cakap-cakap mengenai kerjasama PH-Bersatu kembali kedengaran, kali ini dengan nada lebih serius.
Persoalannya, adakah kedua-dua pihak benar-benar bersedia mengetepikan perseteruan lama, atau gagasan itu sekadar reaksi terhadap kekalahan pilihan raya?
Gesaan itu disuarakan Setiausaha Agung Amanah Faiz Fadzil yang mahu pembentukan 'khemah besar' melibatkan parti di luar PH, khususnya Bersatu, disegerakan menjelang PRU16.

Isyarat hubungan yang semakin mesra turut kelihatan apabila Setiausaha Agung Bersatu Azmin Ali menghadiri Konvensyen Nasional Amanah di Shah Alam, Sabtu lalu, dan dilihat bersama Presidennya Mohamad Sabu.
Namun, Ketua Penerangan Bersatu Tun Faisal Ismail Aziz segera meredakan spekulasi dengan menegaskan kehadiran Azmin sekadar memenuhi undangan Amanah, bukannya petanda kerjasama politik dengan PH.
Walaupun menyifatkan jemputan itu sebagai manifestasi politik matang dan terbuka, Tun Faisal berkata Bersatu hanya bersedia meneroka kerjasama yang tidak mengorbankan prinsip perjuangannya.
Restu pimpinan tertinggi
Di sebalik keterbukaan segelintir pemimpin, persoalan lebih besar ialah sejauh mana gagasan itu mendapat restu kepimpinan tertinggi kedua-dua pihak.
Dalam PH, Amanah kelihatan paling bersungguh-sungguh menggerakkan kerjasama tersebut, namun pendirian DAP berpotensi menjadi penghalang utama.
Penganalisis Tawfik Yaakub berkata pembentukan khemah besar sukar direalisasikan selagi perbezaan dalaman PH belum diselesaikan dan DAP terus menolak kerjasama dengan Bersatu.
Menurutnya, kemenangan DAP di semua empat kerusi PH pada PRN Melaka mengukuhkan kedudukan tawar-menawar parti itu, berbanding Amanah yang gagal memenangi sebarang kerusi.
Malah, Setiausaha Agung DAP Loke Siew Fook menegaskan cadangan berkenaan masih di peringkat Amanah, bukannya keputusan PH, dan sebarang perbincangan sepatutnya dibuat secara dalaman.
Selain perbezaan pendirian, kerjasama itu juga berisiko membuka ruang kepada serangan politik terhadap Bersatu sendiri.
Parti yang sebelum ini menggunakan label 'UmDAP' untuk mengkritik kerjasama Umno dengan DAP mungkin berdepan tuduhan serupa sekiranya memilih untuk berada dalam gabungan yang turut disertai DAP.

Malah, Menteri Besar Perak Saarani Mohamad pernah mengingatkan PAS dan Bersatu mengenai sejarah kerjasama mereka dengan DAP ketika mempertahankan hubungan Umno dengan parti itu daripada sindiran 'UmDAP'.
Justeru, tidak mustahil label 'BersaDAP' kembali menghantui Bersatu sekiranya parti itu memilih untuk kembali bersama PH.
Bagi Bersatu, persoalannya bukan sekadar kesediaan bekerjasama, tetapi bagaimana menjelaskan perubahan pendirian itu kepada akar umbi selepas sekian lama menjadikan DAP sebagai sasaran politik.
Lebih penting, adakah Muhyiddin sendiri bersedia membawa Bersatu kembali bersama PH, atau keterbukaan yang ditunjukkan ketika ini hanya mencerminkan pandangan sebahagian pemimpin?
Hakikatnya, keperluan PH mencari formula baharu untuk memenangi sokongan Melayu semakin mendesak, tetapi menyatukan parti yang pernah berpecah bukan semudah menggabungkan jumlah undi atau kerusi.
Tanpa persetujuan kepimpinan tertinggi, kesediaan akar umbi dan kesepakatan mengenai hala tuju politik, gagasan khemah besar berisiko kekal sebagai percakapan setiap kali keputusan pilihan raya.
Namun, adakah PH dan Bersatu sanggup membayar harga politik untuk kembali bersama?

7936a1d5242e0abf: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — Malaysia must ensure that its newly elevated strategic partnership with France translates into meaningful technology transfer and industrial development, rather than relegating the country to a supplier of raw materials for Europe’s strategic ambitions, said Citizens International executive director Imran Mohd Rasid.

He said closer cooperation with France could help Malaysia diversify its economy and strengthen its industrial capabilities, but cautioned against agreements that could create new forms of economic dependence.

“Malaysia must avoid becoming a mineral supplier for somebody else’s industrial revolution. We should welcome French investment, but Malaysia must not exchange one form of dependency for another,” he said.

His remarks follow French President Emmanuel Macron’s two-day official visit to Malaysia on November 16 and 17, during which both countries elevated bilateral relations to a Strategic Partnership encompassing critical minerals, defence, energy and advanced technologies.

Among the key developments was a rare earth industrial project involving French company Carester and Malaysia’s Malaco Mining Group, which is expected to begin operations in early 2027. The project will involve extraction and processing in Malaysia, with further refining to be carried out in France.

Imran, who is also an international relations expert specialising in Global South affairs, said the arrangement could benefit Malaysia if it enabled the country to move beyond supplying raw materials and develop its own high-value industries.
“If France wants access to our rare earths, it should also help Malaysia acquire the technology, knowledge and industrial capabilities to become a producer of higher-value products,” he said.

He stressed that Malaysia should sweek substantive technology transfer, greater participation by local companies in separation, refining and downstream manufacturing, and opportunities for Malaysian workers and suppliers to undertake higher-value activities.
He also cautioned against environmental risks associated with rare earth extraction and processing, particularly waste management and pollution.

The Malaysian government has maintained its moratorium on raw rare earth exports, which took effect on Jan 1, 2024, while allowing limited and conditional exports for research, development and processing purposes.

Deputy Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Syed Ibrahim Syed Noh told the Dewan Rakyat on Thursday that cooperation with France would focus on technological expertise and developing the entire rare earth value chain, from mining and processing to high-value products.

Imran said the timing of Macron’s visit also reflected growing European concerns over strategic vulnerabilities, with the war in Ukraine, energy insecurity and geopolitical tensions exposing Europe’s dependence on external suppliers for critical minerals, energy and technology.
He said Europe’s growing interest in the Global South could give developing countries greater bargaining power.
On the shared emphasis by Malaysia and France on strategic autonomy, Imran said the concept must be understood in the context of their vastly different economic and geopolitical positions.

He said while France viewed strategic autonomy primarily as a means of protecting its international position and reducing vulnerabilities, Malaysia needed to pursue it as a strategy to overcome structural economic dependencies and strengthen its own development capabilities. — Bernama

797d55e6415146b1: Don't mind the recent arrests. The ShinyHunters extortion gang may still be operating, just under the new name of Inception, according to Okta's threat intelligence group.

ShinyHunters is the brash cybercriminal group that, most recently, breached rival gang Clop before hacking the FBI, resulting in at least three arrests of key suspects in September and October. The crims - and their old data leak site - have since gone dark.

“While this threat cluster has changed their brand affiliation, the operators remain active in targeting organizations with voice phishing attacks and account takeovers resulting in data theft and extortion,” Okta threat hunters Moussa Diallo and Katie Nickels said on Monday.
Okta tracks this threat cluster as O-UNC-053 - the “O-UNC” prefix stands for an Okta Uncategorized cluster, and it uses this label before formally attributing the activity to a named threat group.

While Okta hasn't formally confirmed O-UNC-053 to be the same crime crew as ShinyHunters, the identity and access management provider’s researchers note that it does use nearly identical social engineering tactics: voice phishing, during which the scammers trick targets into entering credentials into phishing pages and approving multi-factor authentication (MFA).

Plus, they note: O-UNC-053 operators change the themes of their phishing domains about every four to six weeks, and they also post claimed victims on ShinyHunters’ data leak site. In November, however, organizations targeted by O-UNC-053 began appearing on a new data leak site branded as Inception and not ShinyHunters.

The first five - Advanced Micro Devices, Cigna Healthcare, Paychex, PepsiCo, and Henry Schein - appeared November 17 on the site, and all were marked “leaked.” Soon after, security maven Dominic Alvieri questioned if Inception was linked to ShinyHunters. “ShinyHunters are not all in jail,” he wrote on social media.
On November 19, AutoZone appeared on the site, with Inception again claiming to have leaked the auto-parts retailer's files. On Saturday, EV technology firm Lucid Group joined the claimed victims.
None of the seven companies have confirmed breaches, and none responded to The Register’s inquiries. We will update this story when we receive more information.
Okta Threat Intelligence “is unable to validate if published data is authentic,” the researchers said in response to our questions.

In the Monday report, the Okta team does note that Inception’s new data leak site listings “included multiple targets for which Okta Threat Intelligence previously observed O-UNC-053 infrastructure registration.”

The infrastructure was registered between six and 19 days before Inception listed the companies on its leak site, and this gap “is consistent with prior shifts from Com-affiliated actors,” Diallo and Nickels added.

The Com (short for community) is a loosely knit network of online groups whose young members participate in a range of illicit activities including hacking, swatting, digital extortion, real-life shootings, and other physical violence. Many security researchers consider ShinyHunters to be connected to The Com, along with groups such as Scattered Spider and LAPSUS$, with overlapping memberships and shared infrastructure.

“Before and after the change in DLS publication, O-UNC-053 maintained consistent infrastructure and TTPs, leading us to assess that the cluster has very likely changed their brand affiliation,” the Okta researchers wrote. “We cannot currently make a high confidence assessment as to whether O-UNC-053 is operating the DLS themselves or is partnering with another extortion actor.”

Regardless, members of the group formerly known as ShinyHunters and/or O-UNC-053 are still roaming the internet, looking for new victims, and conducting voice phishing attacks to steal data and then extort victims' companies for exorbitant sums of money. Consider yourself warned - and turn on phishing-resistant MFA.®
